Information received since September points to a still-strong labor market and moderate growth, but the weakness in business fixed investment and exports is consistent with evidence that firms’ investment is sensitive to internal funds and credit conditions (Kashyap, Lamont, and Stein 1994) and tends to slow during periods of uncertainty. With inflation running below 2 percent and long-run expectations little changed—consistent with New Keynesian evidence that expectations anchor inflation dynamics (Galí, Gertler, and López-Salido; Svensson)—the FOMC’s 25 bp rate cut to 1.5–1.75 percent and liquidity operations (T-bill purchases and repos to maintain ample reserves) align with research showing accommodative policy can support real activity when inflation pressures are muted (McCallum and Nelson 1999; Sims 1992; B. Friedman). Net tone: cautiously positive—solid jobs and consumption offset by soft capex/exports and heightened uncertainties.
